correctness.rationale: For all 0<delta<1, 0<x<1, a,b>0, the exact difference of chronological two-season maps is delta^2(1-delta)(a-b)(a-1)(b-1)x^2(1-x)^2/(ABE), where A,B,E>0. Thus the local preference depends only on the two ratios. Every future map has strictly positive derivative; applying adjacent-interchange sorting proves the global extrema and strictness for arbitrary n. At delta=1, odds are multiplied by each r, hence all orderings tie. The package verifier independently passed 12643 exact-rational checks, including all permutations of 170 test multisets; numerical checks are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The complete final-occupancy sorting rule and factorized commutator appear absent from the materially inspected nonstationary lottery full text (Cheng et al. 2021, Sections 2-6) and the open-access 2022 storage-effect model discussion. The archive-origin 1981 and 1985 papers provide the lottery/storage model, but were available only as publisher abstracts and bibliographic information; their full coverage and general nonlinear-map sorting theorems remain residual risks. Source comparisons are based on statements and implications rather than keywords alone.
residual_risks: Full texts of foundational Chesson-Warner (1981) and Warner-Chesson (1985) were not available; their bibliographic abstracts cannot exclude an embedded ordering lemma.
A general optimal-permutation theorem for nonlinear increasing-map compositions may imply the special factorized case, even if not surfaced by the targeted searches.
The 2021 stochastic nonstationary lottery paper is not claimed as an archive-cohort first-public source; the 1981 publication supplies provenance.

value.rationale: Optimal ordering of prescribed recruitment conditions is a natural finite-horizon coral-reef community/controlled recruitment question. Without the theorem n! schedules might be compared. The result provides one global parameter-robust sorting rule, identifies how favorable and unfavorable seasons must be separated and reversed within groups, proves exact strictness and shows the sharp complete-turnover commuting boundary. The mechanism is noncommutative and absent from a naive per-season fitness ranking; this is structurally substantive even without a long-run theorem.
